bottom_line: UK diverges from EU on AI regulation and chemical safety standards, creating dual-compliance burden for firms operating in both markets.
what_changed: UK government published its own AI regulatory framework rejecting the EU's risk-based approach in favor of sector-specific regulation.
why_it_matters: Companies must maintain separate compliance programs for UK and EU markets; cost and complexity increase for cross-border operations.
main_uncertainty: UK framework is principles-based and largely unlegislated; actual compliance requirements depend on sector regulators.

scenarios.name: Pragmatic alignment
scenarios.description: UK regulators adopt requirements functionally similar to EU despite different framing.
indicators: Cross-referencing of EU standards in UK guidance

scenarios.name: Deepening divergence
scenarios.description: UK deliberately differentiates to attract investment; compliance arbitrage opportunities emerge.

watch_next: UK sector regulator AI guidance publications
